verses.1:1: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem and laid siege to it.
verses.1:2: And the Lord gave Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into his hand, along with a portion of the vessels of the house of God; and he carried them into the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and he brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.
verses.1:3: And the king spoke to Ashpenaz, his chief eunuch, to bring in some of the sons of the captivity of Israel, both from the royal seed and from the Phorthommin,
verses.1:4: young men in whom there was no blemish, handsome in appearance, having understanding in all wisdom, possessing knowledge, and discerning prudence, and who had strength in them to stand in the house of the king, and to teach them the writings and language of the Chaldeans.
verses.1:5: And the king appointed for them a daily portion, day by day, from the table of the king and from the wine that he drank, and to nourish them for three years, and after these things to stand before the king.
verses.1:6: And among them, from the sons of Judah, were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
verses.1:7: And the chief eunuch assigned names to them: to Daniel, Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
verses.1:8: And Daniel set it upon his heart that he would not defile himself with the table of the king or with the wine that he drank, and he petitioned the chief eunuch that he might not defile himself.
verses.1:9: And God granted Daniel mercy and compassion before the chief eunuch.
verses.1:10: And the chief eunuch said to Daniel, "I fear my lord the king, who has appointed your food and your drink, lest he see your countenances downcast compared to the youths of your own age, and you bring condemnation upon my head before the king."
verses.1:11: And Daniel said to Amelsad, whom the chief eunuch had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:
verses.1:12: "Test your servants now for ten days, and let them give us some of the seeds, and we will eat, and we will drink water;
verses.1:13: and let our appearances be observed before you, along with the appearances of the youths who eat from the table of the king; and according to what you see, do with your servants."
verses.1:14: And he listened to them, and tested them for ten days.
verses.1:15: And after the end of the ten days, their appearances were seen to be better, and they were stronger in flesh than the youths who ate from the table of the king.
verses.1:16: And Amelsad continually took away their meal and the wine of their drinking, and gave them seeds.
verses.1:17: And as for these youths, the four of them, God gave them understanding and insight in all learning and wisdom; and Daniel had understanding in every vision and in dreams.
verses.1:18: And after the end of the days when the king had said to bring them in, the chief eunuch brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.1:19: And the king spoke with them, and among all of them none were found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah; and they stood before the king.
verses.1:20: And in every matter of wisdom and knowledge about which the king inquired of them, he found them ten times superior to all the enchanters and the magicians who were in all his kingdom.
verses.1:21: And Daniel remained until the first year of Cyrus the king.
verses.2:1: In the second year of the reign, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed a dream, and his spirit was deeply troubled, and his sleep departed from him.
verses.2:2: And the king commanded to summon the enchanters, and the magicians, and the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans, to declare to the king his dreams; and they came and stood before the king.
verses.2:3: And the king said to them, "I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is distraught to know the dream."
verses.2:4: And the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Syriac, "O king, live forever! Tell the dream to your servants, and we will declare the interpretation."
verses.2:5: The king answered the Chaldeans, "The word has departed from me; if you do not make known to me the dream and the interpretation, you shall come to destruction, and your houses shall be plundered.
verses.2:6: But if you make known to me the dream and its interpretation, gifts and rewards and great honor you shall receive from me; only declare to me the dream and its interpretation."
verses.2:7: They answered a second time and said, "Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will declare its interpretation."
verses.2:8: And the king answered and said, "Of a truth I know that you are buying time, because you saw that the word has departed from me.
verses.2:9: If therefore you do not declare the dream to me, I know that you have conspired to speak a false and corrupt word before me until the time passes by; tell me my dream, and I shall know that you will declare to me its interpretation."
verses.2:10: The Chaldeans answered before the king and say, "There is not a man upon the dry land who shall be able to make known the king's matter, because no great king or ruler asks such a thing of any enchanter, magician, or Chaldean;
verses.2:11: for the matter which the king asks is grievous, and there is no other who shall declare it before the king except the gods, whose dwelling is not with all flesh."
verses.2:12: Then the king in wrath and anger commanded to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:13: And the decree went forth, and the wise men were being slain; and they sought Daniel and his companions to slay them.
verses.2:14: Then Daniel answered with counsel and judgment to Arioch, the chief captain of the king's guard, who had gone forth to slay the wise men of Babylon,
verses.2:15: "Captain of the king, why has the harsh decree gone forth from the presence of the king?" And Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.
verses.2:16: And Daniel petitioned the king that he would grant him time, and he would declare its interpretation to the king.
verses.2:17: And Daniel went into his house and made the matter known to Hananiah, and to Mishael, and to Azariah his companions;
verses.2:18: and they sought compassions from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, that Daniel and his companions might not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:19: Then to Daniel in a vision of the night the mystery was revealed. And Daniel blessed the God of heaven,
verses.2:20: and said, "May the name of God be blessed from everlasting and to everlasting, for wisdom and understanding are His;
verses.2:21: and He changes times and seasons; He sets up kings and removes them, giving wisdom to the wise and discernment to those who know understanding;
verses.2:22: He reveals deep and hidden things, knowing what is in the darkness, and the light abides with Him.
verses.2:23: To You, O God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, for You have given me wisdom and might, and have made known to me the things which we requested of You; yes, the vision of the king You have made known to me."
verses.2:24: And Daniel came to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, "Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon, but bring me in before the king, and I will declare the interpretation to the king."
verses.2:25: Then Arioch in haste brought Daniel in before the king and said to him, "I have found a man of the sons of the captivity of Judea, who will declare the interpretation to the king."
verses.2:26: And the king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, "Are you able to declare to me the dream which I saw, and its interpretation?"
verses.2:27: And Daniel answered before the king and says, "The mystery which the king asks, it is not in the power of wise men, magicians, enchanters, or diviners to declare to the king;
verses.2:28: rather, there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and He has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar the things which must come to pass in the last days. Your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed are this:
verses.2:29: O king, your thoughts upon your bed arose as to what must come to pass hereafter, and He who reveals mysteries has made known to you what must come to pass.
verses.2:30: And to me, not by any wisdom that is in me more than all the living has this mystery been revealed, but for the sake of making known the interpretation to the king, that you may know the thoughts of your heart.
verses.2:31: You, O king, were beholding, and behold, one image; great was that image, and its appearance surpassing, standing before your face, and its aspect was terrible.
verses.2:32: An image whose head was of fine gold, its hands and breast and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze,
verses.2:33: its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of earthenware.
verses.2:34: You were beholding until a stone was broken away out of a mountain without hands, and it struck the image upon its feet of iron and earthenware, and ground them to powder utterly.
verses.2:35: Then were ground to powder all at once the earthenware, the iron, the bronze, the silver, and the gold, and it became like dust from a summer threshing floor; and the force of the wind carried them away, and no place was found for them; and the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled all the earth.
verses.2:36: This is the dream; and its interpretation we will tell before the king.
verses.2:37: You, O king, are a king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given a strong and mighty and honorable kingdom
verses.2:38: in every place where the sons of men dwell; both wild beasts of the field and birds of heaven He has given into your hand, and has set you as lord of all; you are the head of gold.
verses.2:39: And after you shall arise another kingdom inferior to you, and a third kingdom which is the bronze, which shall have dominion over all the earth;
verses.2:40: and a fourth kingdom shall be strong as the iron; in like manner as iron grinds to powder and subdues all things, so shall it grind to powder and subdue all things.
verses.2:41: And whereas you saw the feet and the toes partly of earthenware and partly of iron, it shall be a divided kingdom, yet of the root of iron there shall be in it, in like manner as you saw the iron mingled with the earthenware.
verses.2:42: And as the toes of the feet were partly of iron and partly of earthenware, a part of the kingdom shall be strong, and a part of it shall be shattered.
verses.2:43: Whereas you saw the iron mingled with the earthenware, they shall be mingled in the seed of men; yet they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron does not mingle with earthenware.
verses.2:44: And in the days of those kings shall the God of heaven raise up a kingdom which to the ages shall not be destroyed, and His kingdom shall not be left to another people; it shall grind to powder and winnow all the kingdoms, and itself shall stand to the ages,
verses.2:45: in like manner as you saw that out of a mountain a stone was cut without hands, and it ground to powder the earthenware, the iron, the bronze, the silver, and the gold. The great God has made known to the king what must come to pass hereafter; and true is the dream, and faithful its interpretation."
verses.2:46: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell upon his face and bowed down to Daniel, and commanded to offer manna and sweet savors to him.
verses.2:47: And the king answered and said to Daniel, "Of a truth your God, He is God of gods and Lord of kings, and a revealer of mysteries, seeing you have been able to reveal this mystery."
verses.2:48: And the king magnified Daniel, and gave him great and many gifts, and set him over all the province of Babylon and as chief of satraps over all the wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:49: And Daniel made request of the king, and he set over the affairs of the province of Babylon Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego; and Daniel remained in the court of the king.
verses.3:1: In the eighteenth year, Nebuchadnezzar the king made a golden image, its height sixty cubits and its breadth six cubits; and he set it up on the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.
verses.3:2: And he sent to gather together the chief magistrates, the commanders, and the governors, the leaders, the lords, those in authority, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image which he had set up.
verses.3:3: And the governors, chief magistrates, commanders, leaders, great lords, those in authority, and all the rulers of the provinces were gathered together to the dedication of the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; and they stood before the image.
verses.3:4: And the herald cried aloud with might, "To you it is declared, O peoples, tribes, and tongues,
verses.3:5: at whatever hour you hear the sound of the trumpet, pipe and lyre, harp and psaltery, and every kind of music, fall down and worship the golden image which Nebuchadnezzar the king has set up;
verses.3:6: and whoever does not worship shall in that very hour be cast into the burning furnace of fire."
verses.3:7: And it came to pass, when the peoples heard the sound of the trumpet, pipe and lyre, harp and psaltery, and every kind of music, all the peoples, tribes, and tongues fell down and worshiped the golden image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.
verses.3:8: Then Chaldean men came forward and accused the Jews to the king,
verses.3:10: You, O king, have issued a decree that every man who hears the sound of the trumpet, pipe and lyre, harp and psaltery, and every kind of music,
verses.3:11: and does not fall down and worship the golden image, shall be cast into the burning furnace of fire.
verses.3:12: There are Jewish men whom you have appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—who have not obeyed your decree, O king; they do not serve your gods, nor do they worship the golden image which you have set up."
verses.3:13: Then Nebuchadnezzar, in wrath and fury, gave command to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego; and they were brought before the king.
verses.3:14: And Nebuchadnezzar answered and said to them, "Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods, nor worship the golden image which I have set up?
verses.3:15: Now therefore, if you are ready, so that as soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, pipe and lyre, harp, psaltery, and symphony, and every kind of music, you fall down and worship the image which I have made—but if you do not worship, in that very hour you shall be cast into the burning furnace of fire. And who is the god who will deliver you out of my hand?"
verses.3:16: And Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered, saying to King Nebuchadnezzar, "We have no need to answer you concerning this matter.
verses.3:17: For there is a God whom we serve, who is able to deliver us from the burning furnace of fire; and He will rescue us out of your hands, O king.
verses.3:18: And if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we do not serve your gods, nor do we worship the image which you have set up."
verses.3:19: Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with wrath, and the expression of his countenance was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego; and he commanded to heat the furnace sevenfold, until it was heated to the utmost.
verses.3:20: And he commanded men mighty in strength to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and to cast them into the burning furnace of fire.
verses.3:21: Then those men were bound in their trousers, turbans, and leggings, and were cast into the midst of the burning furnace of fire,
verses.3:22: because the word of the king prevailed, and the furnace was heated exceedingly.
verses.3:23: And these three, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell down bound into the midst of the burning furnace.
verses.3:24: And they walked about in the midst of the flame, singing hymns to God and blessing the Lord.
verses.3:25: And Azariah stood up and prayed in this manner; and opening his mouth in the midst of the fire, he said:
verses.3:26: "Blessed are You, O Lord God of our fathers, and worthy of praise, and Your name is glorified forever.
verses.3:27: For You are righteous in all that You have done, and all Your works are true, and Your ways are upright, and all Your judgments are truth.
verses.3:28: And You have executed judgments of truth according to all that You have brought upon us and upon the holy city of our fathers, Jerusalem; for in truth and judgment You have brought all these things because of our sins.
verses.3:29: For we have sinned and acted lawlessly in departing from You, and we have grievously sinned in all things; and we have not heeded Your commandments,
verses.3:30: nor have we kept them, nor have we done as You commanded us, that it might go well with us.
verses.3:31: And all that You have brought upon us, and all that You have done to us, You have done in true judgment.
verses.3:32: And You have delivered us into the hands of lawless enemies and most hateful rebels, and to an unjust king, the most wicked in all the earth.
verses.3:33: And now we cannot open our mouth; shame and reproach have come upon Your servants and upon those who worship You.
verses.3:34: Do not deliver us up utterly, for Your name's sake, and do not annul Your covenant,
verses.3:35: and do not withdraw Your mercy from us, for the sake of Abraham who is beloved by You, and for the sake of Isaac Your servant, and Israel Your holy one,
verses.3:36: to whom You spoke that You would multiply their seed as the stars of heaven and as the sand along the shore of the sea.
verses.3:37: For, O Master, we have been made smaller than all the nations, and we are brought low in all the earth this day because of our sins.
verses.3:38: And there is at this time neither ruler, nor prophet, nor leader, nor burnt offering, nor sacrifice, nor oblation, nor incense, nor place to present an offering before You and find mercy.
verses.3:39: Yet with a contrite soul and a spirit of humility may we be accepted; as with a burnt offering of rams and bulls, and with ten thousands of fat lambs,
verses.3:40: so let our sacrifice be before You this day, and may we wholly follow after You; for there shall be no shame for those who trust in You.
verses.3:41: And now we follow You with all our heart, and we fear You and seek Your face. Do not put us to shame,
verses.3:42: but deal with us according to Your forbearance and according to the multitude of Your mercy.
verses.3:43: And deliver us according to Your wondrous works, and give glory to Your name, O Lord.
verses.3:44: And let all those who do evil to Your servants be confounded, and let them be put to shame from all power, and let their strength be broken;
verses.3:45: let them know that You are the Lord, the only God, and glorious over all the inhabited earth."
verses.3:46: And the king's servants who had cast them in did not cease stoking the furnace with naphtha, pitch, tow, and brushwood.
verses.3:47: And the flame streamed forth forty-nine cubits above the furnace,
verses.3:48: and it broke forth and burned up those of the Chaldeans whom it found around the furnace.
verses.3:49: But the angel of the Lord came down into the furnace together with Azariah and his companions, and drove the flame of the fire out of the furnace,
verses.3:50: and made the midst of the furnace like a whistling breeze of dew; and the fire did not touch them at all, neither did it hurt nor trouble them.
verses.3:51: Then the three, as out of one mouth, sang hymns and glorified and blessed God in the furnace, saying:
verses.3:52: "Blessed are You, O Lord God of our fathers, and worthy of praise and exalted above all forever. And blessed is the holy name of Your glory, and supremely worthy of praise and exalted above all to all ages.
verses.3:53: Blessed are You in the temple of Your holy glory, and supremely extolled and supremely glorious forever.
verses.3:54: Blessed are You upon the throne of Your kingdom, and supremely extolled and exalted above all forever.
verses.3:55: Blessed are You who behold the depths, sitting upon the cherubim, and worthy of praise and exalted above all forever.
verses.3:56: Blessed are You in the firmament of heaven, and extolled and glorified forever.
verses.3:57: Bless the Lord, all works of the Lord; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:58: Bless the Lord, angels of the Lord; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:59: Bless the Lord, O heavens; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:60: Bless the Lord, waters and all things above the heaven; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:61: Let every power bless the Lord; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:62: Bless the Lord, sun and moon; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:63: Bless the Lord, stars of heaven; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:64: Let every shower and dew bless the Lord; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:65: Bless the Lord, all winds; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:66: Bless the Lord, fire and heat; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:71: Bless the Lord, nights and days; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:72: Bless the Lord, light and darkness; praise and exalt Him above all forever. Bless the Lord, cold and heat; praise and exalt Him above all forever. Bless the Lord, frost and snow; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:73: Bless the Lord, lightnings and clouds; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:74: Let the earth bless the Lord; let it praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:75: Bless the Lord, mountains and hills; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:76: Bless the Lord, all things that grow upon the earth; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:77: Bless the Lord, O springs; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:78: Bless the Lord, seas and rivers; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:79: Bless the Lord, great sea creatures and all things that move in the waters; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:80: Bless the Lord, all birds of heaven; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:81: Bless the Lord, all wild beasts and cattle; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:82: Bless the Lord, O sons of men; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:83: Bless the Lord, O Israel; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:84: Bless the Lord, O priests; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:85: Bless the Lord, O servants; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:86: Bless the Lord, spirits and souls of the righteous; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:87: Bless the Lord, holy ones and humble of heart; praise and exalt Him above all forever.
verses.3:88: Bless the Lord, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael; praise and exalt Him above all forever; for He has delivered us from Hades, and saved us from the hand of death, and rescued us from the midst of the furnace of burning flame, and from the midst of the fire He has rescued us.
verses.3:89: Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures forever.
verses.3:90: Bless the God of gods, all you who worship the Lord; sing praise and give thanks, for His mercy endures forever."
verses.3:91: And Nebuchadnezzar heard them singing hymns and marveled, and he rose up in haste and said to his nobles, "Did we not cast three men bound into the midst of the fire?" And they said to the king, "Truly, O king."
verses.3:92: "Behold, I see four men unbound and walking about in the midst of the fire, and there is no harm in them, and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of God."
verses.3:93: Then Nebuchadnezzar drew near to the door of the burning furnace of fire and said, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out and come here." And Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out from the midst of the fire.
verses.3:94: And the satraps, the commanders, the governors, and the king's potentates gathered together, and they beheld the men, that the fire had no power over their bodies, and the hair of their heads was not scorched, nor were their trousers altered, nor was there the smell of fire upon them.
verses.3:95: And Nebuchadnezzar answered and said, "Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent His angel and delivered His servants, because they trusted in Him; and they set aside the word of the king and yielded up their bodies to the fire, that they might not serve nor worship any god except their own God.
verses.3:96: And I set forth this decree: Every people, tribe, and tongue—if any speaks blasphemy against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, they shall come to destruction, and their houses to plunder; because there is no other god who is able to rescue in this manner."
verses.3:97: Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon, and deemed them worthy to rule over all the Jews who were in his kingdom.
verses.4:4: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and flourishing.
verses.4:5: I saw a dream and it filled me with dread, and I was troubled upon my bed, and the visions of my head greatly disturbed me.
verses.4:10: Upon my bed I was looking, and behold, a tree in the midst of the earth, and its height was great.
verses.4:11: The tree grew large and became strong, and its height reached to heaven, and its expanse to the end of all the earth.
verses.4:12: Its leaves were fair and its fruit was abundant, and in it was food for all; and beneath it the wild beasts took shelter, and in its branches the birds of heaven dwelt, and from it all flesh was nourished.
verses.4:13: I was looking in a vision of the night upon my bed, and behold, a watcher and a holy one came down from heaven.
verses.4:14: And he cried out with might and spoke thus: "Cut down the tree, and tear off its branches, and shake off its leaves, and scatter its fruit; let the beasts be driven from beneath it, and the birds from its branches.
verses.4:15: Nevertheless, leave the stump of its roots in the earth, and in a band of iron and bronze, and in the green grass outside; and in the dew of heaven he shall make his bed, and with the beasts shall be his portion in the grass of the earth.
verses.4:16: His heart shall be changed from that of men, and the heart of a beast shall be given to him, and seven times shall pass over him.
verses.4:17: By the decree of the watchers is this word, and the demand is the utterance of the holy ones, so that the living may know that the Most High is Lord of the kingdom of men, and to whomever He pleases He will give it, and the most despised of men He will set up over it."
verses.4:18: This is the dream which I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw; now you, Belteshazzar, declare the interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make known its interpretation to me; but you, Daniel, are able, for the Holy Spirit of God is in you.
verses.4:19: Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was struck speechless for about one hour, and his thoughts greatly troubled him. And Belteshazzar answered and said, "My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies.
verses.4:20: The tree which you saw, which grew large and became strong, whose height reached to heaven and its expanse to all the earth,
verses.4:21: and its leaves were flourishing and its fruit was abundant, and in it was food for all; beneath it the wild beasts dwelt, and in its branches the birds of heaven took shelter—
verses.4:22: it is you, O king; for you have grown great and become strong, and your greatness has grown and reached to heaven, and your dominion to the ends of the earth.
verses.4:23: And because the king saw a watcher and a holy one coming down from heaven, and he said, 'Tear down the tree and destroy it, nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the earth, and in a band of iron and bronze, and in the green grass outside; and in the dew of heaven he shall lodge, and with wild beasts shall be his portion until seven times pass over him'—
verses.4:24: this is its interpretation, O king, and it is the decree of the Most High which has come upon my lord the king:
verses.4:25: they shall drive you out from among men, and your dwelling shall be with wild beasts, and they shall feed you grass like an ox, and in the dew of heaven you shall lodge, and seven times shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of men, and to whomever He pleases He will give it.
verses.4:26: And because they said, 'Leave the stump of the roots of the tree,' your kingdom shall remain yours from the time that you come to know the heavenly sovereignty.
verses.4:27: Therefore, O king, let my counsel be pleasing to you, and redeem your sins by deeds of mercy, and your iniquities by compassion toward the poor; perhaps God will be longsuffering toward your transgressions."
verses.4:28: All these things came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.4:29: After twelve months, as he was walking upon the palace of his kingdom in Babylon,
verses.4:30: the king answered and said, "Is this not Babylon the great, which I myself have built for a house of the kingdom, by the might of my strength, for the honor of my glory?"
verses.4:31: While the word was still in the mouth of the king, a voice came from heaven: "To you they speak, O King Nebuchadnezzar: the kingdom has passed away from you,
verses.4:32: and from among men they are driving you out, and your dwelling shall be with wild beasts, and they shall feed you grass like an ox, and seven times shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of men, and to whomever He pleases He will give it."
verses.4:33: In that very hour the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar, and he was driven out from among men, and he ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like that of lions and his nails like those of birds.
verses.4:34: And after the end of the days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and glorified Him who lives forever, for His dominion is an everlasting dominion, and His kingdom is from generation to generation.
verses.4:36: At that very time my understanding returned to me, and I came into the honor of my kingdom; and my countenance returned to me, and my rulers and my nobles sought me out, and I was firmly established over my kingdom, and even greater majesty was added to me.
verses.4:37: King Nebuchadnezzar, to all peoples, tribes, and languages who dwell in all the earth: Peace be multiplied to you. It has seemed good before me to declare to you the signs and wonders which the Most High God has done with me. How great and mighty they are! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and His dominion is from generation to generation. Now therefore I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and highly exalt and glorify the King of heaven, for all His works are true and His paths are justice, and all those who walk in pride He is able to humble.
verses.5:1: King Belshazzar made a great feast for his thousand nobles, and before the thousand was the wine.
verses.5:2: And while drinking, Belshazzar commanded at the taste of his wine to bring the gold and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had brought out from the temple in Jerusalem, that the king and his nobles and his concubines and his wives might drink from them.
verses.5:3: So the gold and silver vessels were brought which he had brought out from the temple of God in Jerusalem, and the king and his nobles and his concubines and his wives drank from them.
verses.5:4: They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold and silver and bronze and iron and wood and stone.
verses.5:5: In that very hour fingers of a man's hand came forth and wrote opposite the lamp upon the plaster of the wall and house of the king, and the king watched the joints of the hand that was writing.
verses.5:6: Then the king's countenance changed, and his thoughts greatly troubled him, and the joints of his loins were loosened, and his knees struck against one another.
verses.5:7: And the king cried aloud to bring in the magicians, the Chaldeans, and the astrologers; and he spoke to the wise men of Babylon: "Whoever reads this writing and makes known the interpretation to me shall be clothed in purple, and the golden chain shall be upon his neck, and he shall rule as third in my kingdom."
verses.5:8: Then all the wise men of the king came in, and they were not able to read the writing, nor to make known the interpretation to the king.
verses.5:9: And King Belshazzar was troubled, and his countenance changed within him, and his nobles were thrown into confusion.
verses.5:10: And the queen entered into the banqueting house and said, "O king, live forever! Do not let your thoughts trouble you, and do not let your countenance be changed.
verses.5:11: There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the Spirit of God, and in the days of your father watchfulness and understanding were found in him, and King Nebuchadnezzar your father appointed him chief of the enchanters, magicians, Chaldeans, and astrologers,
verses.5:12: because an extraordinary spirit is in him, and wisdom and understanding—Daniel, who interprets dreams and declares riddles and loosens knots, and the king gave him the name Belteshazzar. Now therefore let him be called, and he will declare its interpretation to you."
verses.5:13: Then Daniel was brought in before the king, and the king said to Daniel, "Are you Daniel, who is of the sons of the captivity of Judea, whom the king my father brought?
verses.5:16: And I have heard concerning you that you are able to interpret judgments; now therefore, if you are able to read the writing and make known its interpretation to me, you shall be clothed in purple, and the golden chain shall be upon your neck, and you shall rule as third in my kingdom."
verses.5:17: And Daniel said before the king, "Let your gifts be for yourself, and give the gift of your house to another; yet I will read the writing and make known its interpretation to you. And this is the writing that has been inscribed: Mane, Thekel, Phares.
verses.5:23: And against the Lord God of heaven you have lifted yourself up, and you have brought the vessels of His house before you, and you and your nobles and your concubines and your wives drank wine from them; and you praised the gods of gold and silver and bronze and iron and wood and stone, which do not see and which do not hear and do not know; and the God in whose hand is your breath and all your ways, Him you have not glorified.
verses.5:26: This is the interpretation of the word: Mane—God has measured your kingdom and brought it to completion;
verses.5:27: Thekel—it has been weighed in the balance and found lacking;
verses.5:28: Phares—your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and Persians."
verses.5:29: Then Belshazzar gave the command, and they clothed Daniel with purple, and placed the golden chain around his neck, and he proclaimed concerning him that he should be the third ruler in the kingdom.
verses.5:30: In that very night Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans was slain.
verses.6:1: And Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being sixty-two years old.
verses.6:2: And it pleased Darius, and he appointed over the kingdom one hundred and twenty satraps, that they should be throughout his whole kingdom,
verses.6:3: and over them three overseers, of whom Daniel was one, that the satraps might render an account to them, so that the king might not be troubled.
verses.6:4: And Daniel was above them, because an extraordinary spirit was in him; and the king appointed him over his whole kingdom.
verses.6:5: And the overseers and the satraps sought to find a pretext against Daniel; yet they found no pretext, nor offense, nor fault against him, because he was faithful.
verses.6:6: And the overseers said, "We shall not find a pretext against Daniel except in the ordinances of his God."
verses.6:7: Then the overseers and the satraps stood before the king and said to him, "O King Darius, live forever!
verses.6:8: All the commanders and satraps, consuls and district governors who are over your kingdom have taken counsel together to establish a royal statute and to confirm an edict, that whoever asks a petition of any god or man for thirty days, except of you, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions.
verses.6:9: Now therefore, O king, establish the edict and issue the writing, so that the decree of the Persians and Medes may not be altered."
verses.6:10: Then King Darius commanded that the decree be written.
verses.6:11: And Daniel, when he knew that the decree had been enacted, went into his house. And his windows were open in his upper chambers toward Jerusalem; and three times a day he knelt upon his knees, praying and giving thanks before his God, just as he had done previously.
verses.6:12: Then those men watched closely, and found Daniel making petition and supplication to his God.
verses.6:13: And approaching, they said to the king, "O king, did you not ordain an edict that every man who asks a petition of any god or man for thirty days, except of you, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions?" And the king said, "The word is true, and the decree of the Medes and Persians shall not pass away."
verses.6:14: Then they answered and said before the king, "Daniel, from the sons of the captivity of Judea, has not submitted to your decree, and three times a day he asks his petitions of his God."
verses.6:15: Then the king, when he heard the word, was greatly grieved over it, and strove earnestly on behalf of Daniel to deliver him.
verses.6:17: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel and cast him into the den of lions; and the king said to Daniel, "Your God, whom you serve continually, He will deliver you."
verses.6:18: And they brought a stone and laid it upon the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his signet ring and with the signet ring of his nobles, so that the matter concerning Daniel might not be altered.
verses.6:19: And the king went away to his house and lay down without supper, and they brought no food to him, and sleep departed from him. And God shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not trouble Daniel.
verses.6:20: Then the king arose early in the morning at daylight, and came in haste to the den of lions.
verses.6:21: And as he drew near to the den, he cried out with a strong voice, "Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to deliver you from the mouth of the lions?"
verses.6:22: And Daniel said to the king, "O king, live forever!
verses.6:23: My God sent His angel and stopped the mouths of the lions, and they did not harm me, because uprightness was found in me before Him; and before you also, O king, I have committed no offense."
verses.6:24: Then the king was exceedingly glad for him, and commanded that Daniel be brought up out of the den. So Daniel was brought up out of the den, and no injury whatever was found on him, because he trusted in his God.
verses.6:25: And the king commanded, and they brought the men who had accused Daniel, and they were cast into the den of lions—they, their sons, and their wives; and they had not reached the bottom of the den before the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones to pieces.
verses.6:26: Then King Darius wrote to all peoples, tribes, and tongues dwelling in all the earth: "May peace be multiplied to you.
verses.6:27: From my presence this decree is set forth, that in every dominion of my kingdom men are to tremble and fear before the God of Daniel; for He is the living God, enduring forever, and His kingdom shall not be destroyed, and His dominion is to the end.
verses.6:28: He helps and rescues, and works signs and wonders in heaven and on earth, who has delivered Daniel from the hand of the lions."
verses.6:29: And Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
verses.7:1: In the third year of Belshazzar king of the Chaldeans, Daniel saw a dream, and the visions of his head upon his bed; and he wrote down his dream.
verses.7:2: I, Daniel, was watching, and behold, the four winds of heaven were beating upon the great sea.
verses.7:3: And four great beasts came up from the sea, differing one from another.
verses.7:4: The first was like a lioness, and she had wings like those of an eagle. I watched until her wings were plucked off, and she was lifted up from the earth and made to stand upon the feet of a man, and the heart of a man was given to her.
verses.7:5: And behold, a second beast, like a bear; and it stood upon one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth. And thus they said to it, "Arise, devour much flesh."
verses.7:6: After this I watched, and behold, another beast, like a leopard; and it had four wings of a bird above it, and the beast had four heads, and authority was given to it.
verses.7:7: After this I watched, and behold, a fourth beast, dreadful and terrifying and exceedingly strong; and its teeth were of iron, devouring and crushing, and it trampled the remainder with its feet. And it was exceedingly different from all the beasts that were before it, and it had ten horns.
verses.7:8: I was considering its horns, and behold, another horn, a little one, came up in the midst of them, and three of the horns that were before it were uprooted from before it; and behold, eyes like the eyes of a man were in this horn, and a mouth speaking great things.
verses.7:9: I watched until thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days was seated. His garment was white as snow, and the hair of His head like pure wool; His throne was a flame of fire, and its wheels were burning fire.
verses.7:10: A river of fire flowed forth before Him; a thousand thousands ministered to Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him. The court was seated, and books were opened.
verses.7:11: I watched then because of the sound of the great words which that horn was speaking, until the beast was slain and perished, and its body was given over to the burning of fire.
verses.7:12: And the dominion of the rest of the beasts was removed, yet length of life was given to them until a time and a time.
verses.7:13: I was watching in a vision of the night, and behold, One like a Son of Man was coming with the clouds of heaven; and He came up to the Ancient of Days, and was brought near before Him.
verses.7:14: And to Him were given the dominion and the honor and the kingdom, and all peoples, tribes, and tongues serve Him. His authority is an everlasting authority, which shall not pass away, and His kingdom shall not be destroyed.
verses.7:15: As for me, Daniel, my spirit shuddered within my frame, and the visions of my head troubled me.
verses.7:16: And I approached one of those who stood by, and sought the exact truth from him concerning all these things. And he told me the exact truth, and made known to me the interpretation of the words:
verses.7:17: "These four beasts are four kingdoms that shall arise upon the earth, which shall be taken away;
verses.7:18: and the saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom and shall possess it forever and ever."
verses.7:19: And I sought exact knowledge concerning the fourth beast, because it was different from every beast, exceedingly dreadful, its teeth of iron and its claws of bronze, devouring and crushing, and it trampled the remainder with its feet;
verses.7:20: and concerning its ten horns that were on its head, and the other horn that came up and shook off some of the first ones, which had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and whose appearance was greater than the rest.
verses.7:21: I watched, and that horn was making war against the saints and prevailed against them,
verses.7:22: until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment to the saints of the Most High, and the time arrived, and the saints possessed the kingdom.
verses.7:23: And he said, "The fourth beast shall be a fourth kingdom on the earth, which shall surpass all the kingdoms, and shall devour the whole earth, and shall trample it down and cut it in pieces.
verses.7:24: And as for its ten horns, ten kings shall arise; and after them shall arise one who shall surpass in evils all those before him, and he shall humble three kings,
verses.7:25: and he shall speak words against the Most High, and shall wear out the saints of the Most High, and shall think to alter times and law; and it shall be given into his hand until a time and times and half a time.
verses.7:26: And the court was seated, and they shall remove the dominion, to consume and to destroy it to the end;
verses.7:27: and the kingdom and the authority and the greatness of the kings under the whole heaven were given to the saints of the Most High. And His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey Him." Thus far is the end of the account.
verses.7:28: As for me, Daniel, my thoughts greatly troubled me, and my countenance was changed; and I kept the matter in my heart.
verses.8:1: In the third year of the reign of Belshazzar the king, a vision appeared to me—I, Daniel—after the one that had appeared to me at the first.
verses.8:2: And I was in Susa the citadel, which is in the region of Elam, and I was by the Ubal.
verses.8:3: And I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, one ram was standing before the Ubal, and he had high horns; and the one was higher than the other, and the high one came up last.
verses.8:4: I saw the ram thrusting toward the sea, and the north, and the south; and none of the beasts could stand before him, nor was there any who could deliver from his hand; and he did according to his will and became great.
verses.8:5: And as I was considering, behold, a male goat came from the west over the face of all the earth, and was not touching the ground; and the goat had a horn between his eyes.
verses.8:6: And he came up to the ram that had the horns, whom I had seen standing before the Ubal, and he ran at him in the fury of his strength.
verses.8:7: And I saw him drawing close to the ram, and he was fiercely enraged against him; and he struck the ram and shattered both of his horns, and there was no strength in the ram to stand before him; and he cast him down to the ground and trampled upon him, and there was none to deliver the ram from his hand.
verses.8:8: And the male goat grew exceedingly great; and when he became strong, his great horn was shattered, and four horns came up beneath it toward the four winds of heaven.
verses.8:9: And out of one of them came forth one strong horn, and it grew exceedingly great toward the south and toward the host;
verses.8:10: it grew great even up to the host of heaven; and some of the host of heaven and of the stars fell to the earth, and they trampled them underfoot,
verses.8:11: even until the Chief Commander delivers the captivity; and because of him sacrifice was dashed down, and it prospered for him; and the sanctuary shall be made desolate.
verses.8:12: And sin was given against the sacrifice, and righteousness was cast down to the ground; and he acted and prospered.
verses.8:13: And I heard a holy one speaking; and one holy one said to Phelmouni who was speaking, "How long shall the vision stand, the sacrifice that was taken away, and the sin of desolation that was given, and the sanctuary and the host be trampled underfoot?"
verses.8:14: And he said to him, "Until evening and morning, two thousand three hundred days; and the sanctuary shall be cleansed."
verses.8:15: And it came to pass, when I, Daniel, saw the vision, that I was seeking understanding; and behold, there stood before me one like the appearance of a man.
verses.8:16: And I heard a man's voice from the midst of the Ubal, and it called and said, "Gabriel, make that man understand the vision."
verses.8:17: And he came and stood near where I was standing; and when he came, I was terrified and fell on my face; and he said to me, "Son of man, for the vision is yet for the end of the appointed time."
verses.8:18: And while he was speaking with me, I fell on my face to the ground; and he touched me and set me on my feet,
verses.8:19: and said, "Behold, I am making known to you the things that shall come to pass at the end of the wrath; for the vision is yet for the end of the appointed time.
verses.8:20: The ram which you saw, having the horns, is the king of the Persians and the Medes.
verses.8:21: And the male goat is the king of the Greeks; and the great horn that was between his eyes—he is the first king.
verses.8:22: And as for the one that was shattered, beneath which four horns stood up, four kings shall arise out of his nation, yet not in their own strength.
verses.8:23: And in the latter time of their kingdom, when their sins have reached their fullness, a king shall arise, shameless of countenance and understanding riddles.
verses.8:24: And mighty shall be his strength, and he shall bring astonishing destruction, and he shall prosper and act, and he shall destroy the mighty and a holy people.
verses.8:25: And the yoke of his collar shall prosper; deceit is in his hand, and in his heart he shall magnify himself, and by deceit he shall destroy many, and he shall stand upon the destruction of many, and like eggs he shall crush them by hand.
verses.8:26: And the vision of the evening and the morning that was spoken is truly so; and as for you, seal up the vision, for it is for many days."
verses.8:27: And I, Daniel, lay down and fell sick; and I arose and performed the king's works, and I marveled at the vision, and there was none who understood it.
verses.9:1: In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, who reigned over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,
verses.9:2: I, Daniel, understood in the books the number of the years concerning which the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, for the fulfillment of the desolation of Jerusalem: seventy years.
verses.9:3: And I set my face toward the Lord God to seek prayer and supplications, in fastings and sackcloth.
verses.9:4: And I prayed to the Lord my God, and made confession, and said, "O Lord, the great and wondrous God, who keeps Your covenant and mercy toward those who love You and those who keep Your commandments:
verses.9:5: we have sinned, we have committed iniquity, we have acted lawlessly, and we have departed and turned aside from Your commandments and from Your judgments;
verses.9:6: and we have not heeded Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings and our rulers and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.
verses.9:7: To You, O Lord, belongs righteousness, and to us belongs shame of face, as on this day—to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, those near and those far off in every land where You have scattered them, because of their unfaithfulness with which they have acted unfaithfully.
verses.9:8: In You, O Lord, is our righteousness, and to us belongs shame of face, and to our kings, and to our rulers, and to our fathers, who have sinned against You.
verses.9:9: To the Lord our God belong compassions and forgiveness, though we have rebelled,
verses.9:10: and we have not heeded the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in His laws which He set before our face by the hands of His servants the prophets.
verses.9:11: And all Israel have transgressed Your law and have turned aside so as not to hear Your voice; and there has come upon us the curse and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of God, because we have sinned against Him.
verses.9:12: And He has established His words which He spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, by bringing upon us great calamities, such as have not been done under the whole heaven like what has been done in Jerusalem.
verses.9:13: As it is written in the law of Moses, all these calamities have come upon us; yet we have not implored the face of the Lord our God, so as to turn from our iniquities and to gain understanding in all Your truth.
verses.9:14: And the Lord kept watch and brought them upon us; for the Lord our God is righteous in all His doing which He has done, yet we have not heeded His voice.
verses.9:15: And now, O Lord our God, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made Yourself a name as on this day—we have sinned, we have acted lawlessly.
verses.9:16: O Lord, in all Your mercy, let Your anger and Your wrath, I pray, be turned away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain; for we have sinned, and because of our iniquities and those of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people have become a reproach among all who are around us.
verses.9:17: And now hear, O Lord our God, the prayer of Your servant and his supplications, and cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary, for Your own sake, O Lord.
verses.9:18: Incline Your ear, O my God, and hear; open Your eyes and behold our desolation, and that of Your city upon which Your name is called; for we do not cast our plea for mercy before You because of our own righteous deeds, but because of Your abundant compassions, O Lord.
verses.9:19: Hear, O Lord; forgive, O Lord; give heed, O Lord; do not delay, for Your own sake, O my God, for Your name is called upon Your city and upon Your people."
verses.9:20: And while I was still speaking and praying, and confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel, and casting my plea for mercy before the Lord my God concerning the holy mountain,
verses.9:21: even while I was still speaking in prayer, behold, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, came flying and touched me about the time of the evening sacrifice.
verses.9:22: And he gave me understanding, and spoke with me and said, "Daniel, now I have come forth to instruct you in understanding.
verses.9:23: At the beginning of your supplication a word went forth, and I have come to declare it to you, for you are a man greatly treasured; therefore consider the word and understand the vision.
verses.9:24: Seventy weeks have been decreed upon your people and upon the holy city, to bring sin to an end, and to seal up sins, and to blot out iniquities, and to make atonement for iniquities, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up vision and prophet, and to anoint a Holy of Holies.
verses.9:25: And you shall know and understand: from the going forth of a word to answer and to build Jerusalem until an Anointed One, a ruler, there shall be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks; and it shall return and be built, both broad street and wall, and the times shall be emptied out.
verses.9:26: And after the sixty-two weeks, an anointing shall be utterly destroyed, and there is no judgment in it; and he shall destroy the city and the sanctuary together with the coming ruler; they shall be cut off in a flood; and until the end of the war that is cut short, desolations are by decree.
verses.9:27: And one week shall confirm a covenant for many; and in the half of the week My sacrifice and drink offering shall be taken away; and upon the temple shall be an abomination of desolations, and until the consummation of the time, a consummation shall be given upon the desolation."
verses.10:1: In the third year of Cyrus king of the Persians, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the word was true, and great power and understanding were given to him in the vision.
verses.10:2: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three weeks of days.
verses.10:3: I ate no choice bread, and neither meat nor wine entered my mouth, nor did I anoint myself with ointment, until the completion of three weeks of days.
verses.10:4: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was beside the great river, which is Tigris Eddekel.
verses.10:5: And I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, one man clothed in baddin, and his waist was girded with gold of Uphaz.
verses.10:6: And his body was like Tarshish, and his face like the appearance of lightning, and his eyes like torches of fire, and his arms and legs like the appearance of gleaming bronze, and the sound of his words like the voice of a multitude.
verses.10:7: And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision, and the men who were with me did not see the vision; rather, a great dread fell upon them, and they fled in fear.
verses.10:8: And I was left alone and saw this great vision, and no strength remained in me; and my glory was turned into corruption, and I retained no strength.
verses.10:9: And I heard the sound of his words; and when I heard him, I was stunned, and my face was toward the ground.
verses.10:10: And behold, a hand touched me and raised me upon my knees.
verses.10:11: And he said to me, "Daniel, greatly desired man, understand the words that I speak to you, and stand in your place, for now I have been sent to you." And while he spoke this word to me, I stood up trembling.
verses.10:12: And he said to me, "Do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to afflict yourself before your God, your words were heard; and I have come because of your words.
verses.10:13: And the prince of the kingdom of the Persians stood opposite me twenty-one days; and behold, Michael, one of the princes, came to help me, and I left him there with the prince of the kingdom of the Persians.
verses.10:14: And I have come to make you understand all that shall befall your people in the last of the days, for the vision is still for days."
verses.10:15: And while he was speaking with me according to these words, I set my face toward the ground.
verses.10:16: And behold, one like the likeness of a son of man touched my lips; and I opened my mouth and spoke, and said to the one standing before me, "O lord, in your vision my inward parts were turned within me, and I had no strength.
verses.10:17: And how shall your servant, O lord, be able to speak with this my lord? As for me, from now on no strength will remain in me, and no breath is left in me."
verses.10:18: Then the one like the appearance of a man touched me again and strengthened me.
verses.10:19: And he said to me, "Do not fear, greatly desired man; peace be to you! Be courageous and be strong." And as he spoke with me, I was strengthened, and said, "Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me."
verses.10:20: And he said, "Do you know why I have come to you? And now I shall return to fight with the prince of the Persians; and I was going in, and the prince of the Greeks was coming.
verses.10:21: Nevertheless, I will declare to you what is recorded in the writing of truth; and there is not one who holds firmly with me concerning these things except Michael your prince."
verses.11:1: "And I, in the first year of Cyrus, stood for might and strength.
verses.11:2: And now I will declare the truth to you: behold, three more kings shall arise in Persia, and the fourth shall acquire great riches above all; and after he takes hold of his riches, he shall rise up against all the kingdoms of the Greeks.
verses.11:3: And a mighty king shall arise, and he shall rule with great dominion, and he shall do according to his will.
verses.11:4: And as soon as he has stood up, his kingdom shall be shattered and divided toward the four winds of heaven, and not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion which he ruled; for his kingdom shall be plucked up, even for others besides these.
verses.11:5: And the king of the south shall grow strong; and one of their princes shall grow strong above them and shall rule a great dominion.
verses.11:6: And after his years they shall join in alliance, and the daughter of the king of the south shall come to the king of the north to make covenants with him; yet she shall not retain the strength of an arm, and his seed shall not stand, and she shall be given up, along with those who bring her, and the young woman, and the one who strengthens her in those times.
verses.11:7: And one shall stand up from the blossom of her root, of his appointed place, and he shall come against the army, and shall enter into the strongholds of the king of the north, and shall deal with them and prevail.
verses.11:8: And also their gods with their molten images, every precious vessel of theirs, of silver and of gold, he shall carry with captivity into Egypt; and he shall stand above the king of the north.
verses.11:9: And he shall enter into the kingdom of the king of the south, and he shall return to his own land.
verses.11:10: And his sons shall gather a multitude in the midst of many; and he shall surely come and overflow, and pass through, and settle down, and contend even to his strength.
verses.11:11: And the king of the south shall be enraged, and shall go forth and fight with the king of the north; and he shall set forth a great multitude, and a multitude shall be given into his hand.
verses.11:12: And he shall take the multitude, and his heart shall be lifted up; and he shall cast down ten thousands, yet he shall not prevail.
verses.11:13: And the king of the north shall return and shall lead a greater multitude than the former; and at the end of the times of years he shall come advancing in great power and with much substance.
verses.11:14: And in those times many shall rise up against the king of the south; and the sons of the remnant of your people shall exalt themselves to establish a vision, and they shall falter.
verses.11:15: And the king of the north shall enter and cast up a siege mound and capture fortified cities; and the arms of the king of the south shall take their stand, and his chosen ones also shall rise up, yet there shall be no strength to stand.
verses.11:16: And the one who comes against him shall do according to his will, and there is no one standing before his face; and he shall stand in the land of Sabir, and it shall be brought to completion in his hand.
verses.11:17: And he shall set his face to enter with the strength of his whole kingdom, and he shall make all things right with him; and he shall give him a daughter of women to destroy her, yet she shall by no means remain, nor shall she be for him.
verses.11:18: And he shall turn his face toward the islands and capture many; and he shall put an end to rulers of their reproach, except that his own reproach shall return upon him.
verses.11:19: And he shall turn his face toward the strength of his own land, and he shall falter and fall, and shall not be found.
verses.11:20: And there shall arise from his root a plant of the kingdom in his appointed place, sending across and exacting the glory of the kingdom; and in those days he shall be shattered, yet neither face to face nor in war.
verses.11:21: He shall stand upon his appointed place; he was despised, and they did not bestow upon him the glory of the kingdom; yet he shall come in prosperity, and shall seize the kingdom by slippery deceits.
verses.11:22: And the arms of the one who overflows shall be overflowed from before his face and shall be shattered, and also the leader of the covenant.
verses.11:23: And from the alliances made with him he shall practice deceit, and he shall go up and prevail over them with a small nation.
verses.11:24: And he shall come in prosperity and into fertile regions, and shall do what neither his fathers nor his fathers' fathers have done; plunder and spoil and substance he shall scatter among them, and against Egypt he shall devise schemes, even until a time.
verses.11:25: And his strength and his heart shall be stirred up against the king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south shall join battle with a great and exceedingly strong army; yet they shall not stand, for they shall devise schemes against him.
verses.11:26: And they shall eat his provisions and shatter him; and he shall overwhelm armies, and many wounded shall fall.
verses.11:27: And as for both kings, their hearts shall be bent on wickedness, and at one table they shall speak lies; yet it shall not prosper, for the end is still for an appointed time.
verses.11:28: And he shall return to his own land with great substance, and his heart shall be against the holy covenant; and he shall act and return to his own land.
verses.11:29: At the appointed time he shall return and come into the south; yet the last shall not be like the first.
verses.11:30: And the Kittim who go forth shall come against him, and he shall be humbled; and he shall turn back and be enraged against the holy covenant, and he shall act; and he shall return and give attention to those who forsake the holy covenant.
verses.11:31: And offspring from him shall arise and profane the sanctuary of dominion, and they shall remove the continual sacrifice, and they shall set up a desolated abomination.
verses.11:32: And those who act lawlessly against the covenant shall entice with slippery deceits; but the people who know their God shall prevail and act.
verses.11:33: And the wise of the people shall understand in many things; yet they shall falter by sword and by flame, by captivity and by plundering for days.
verses.11:34: And when they falter, they shall be helped with a little help; and many shall join themselves to them with slippery deceits.
verses.11:35: And some of those who have understanding shall falter, to refine them by fire, and to choose, and to be revealed, until the time of the end; for it is still for an appointed time.
verses.11:36: And he shall do according to his will; and the king shall be exalted and magnified above every god, and shall speak boastful things, and shall prosper until the wrath is accomplished; for it is coming to completion.
verses.11:37: And he shall have no regard for any god of his fathers, nor for the desire of women, nor shall he have regard for any god; for he shall magnify himself above all.
verses.11:38: And he shall glorify the god Maozein in his place; and a god whom his fathers did not know he shall glorify with gold and silver, and with precious stone and with desirable things.
verses.11:39: And he shall act for the strongholds of the refuges with a foreign god; and he shall multiply glory, and he shall subject many to them, and he shall divide the land for gifts.
verses.11:40: And at the end of time he shall lock horns with the king of the south; and the king of the north shall be gathered against him with chariots and horsemen and with many ships; and they shall enter into the land, and he shall shatter and pass through.
verses.11:41: And he shall enter into the land of Sabaein, and many shall falter; yet these shall be delivered out of his hand: Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the sons of Ammon.
verses.11:42: And he shall stretch out his hand over the land, and the land of Egypt shall not be for deliverance.
verses.11:43: And he shall have dominion over the hidden treasures of gold and of silver, and over all the desirable things of Egypt, and of the Libyans and of the Ethiopians, in their strongholds.
verses.11:44: And reports and urgencies shall trouble him from the east and from the north; and he shall come with great wrath to destroy many.
verses.11:45: And he shall pitch his tent Ephadano between the seas toward the holy mountain of Sabaein; yet he shall come to his portion, and there is no one who rescues him."
verses.12:1: "And at that time Michael shall arise, the great prince who stands over the sons of your people; and there shall be a time of tribulation, tribulation such as has not occurred since a nation came into being on the earth until that time. At that time your people shall be saved, everyone who is written in the book.
verses.12:2: And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall be awakened, these to eternal life, and those to reproach and to eternal shame.
verses.12:3: And those who have understanding shall shine like the brightness of the firmament, and some from among the many righteous like the stars forever and beyond.
verses.12:4: And you, Daniel, shut up the rest and seal the book until the time of the end, until many are taught and knowledge is multiplied."
verses.12:5: And I, Daniel, looked, and behold, two others were standing, one on this side of the bank of the river and one on that side of the bank of the river.
verses.12:6: And one said to the man clothed in linen garments, who was above the water of the river, "How long until the end of the wondrous things which you have spoken?"
verses.12:7: And I heard the man clothed in linen garments, who was above the water of the river, and he lifted up his right hand and his left hand to heaven, and swore by Him who lives forever, "For a time of times and half a time; when the scattering is completed, they shall know all these things."
verses.12:8: And I heard, and did not understand; and I said, "O lord, what shall be the latter end of these things?"
verses.12:9: And he said, "Come, Daniel, for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end,
verses.12:10: when many shall be chosen and made white and refined by fire, and the lawless shall act lawlessly; and the lawless shall not understand, but the discerning shall understand.
verses.12:11: And from the time of the removal of the continual sacrifice—and the abomination of desolation shall be set up—there shall be one thousand two hundred and ninety days.
verses.12:12: Blessed is he who endures and attains to one thousand three hundred and thirty-five days.
verses.12:13: And you, come and rest; for there are yet days until the fulfillment of the end, and you shall rise to your allotted portion at the end of days."

notes.1:3: Theodotion Greek adds "captivity" ("sons of the captivity of Israel") and leaves the Persian loanword for "nobles" untranslated as "Phorthommin."
notes.1:7: The Greek text renders Daniel's Babylonian name as "Baltasar," the same spelling Theodotion uses for King Belshazzar in chapter five.
notes.1:11: Theodotion renders the Hebrew title "ha-melzar" ("the steward" or "guardian") as the personal name "Amelsad" (so also in verse sixteen).
notes.1:12: Greek "spermata" literally means "seeds," representing plant-based foods such as grains, legumes, and vegetables (so also in verse sixteen).
notes.2:5: Greek ho logos ap' emou apeste ('the word has departed from me') reflects Theodotion's rendering of Aramaic azda ('is firm/gone forth') as 'has escaped/departed from me.'
notes.2:14: Greek archimageiros literally means 'chief cook/butcher,' the standard Septuagint title for the royal captain of the guard (Hebrew/Aramaic rab tabbachayya).
notes.2:26: Greek transliterates Daniel's Babylonian name as Baltasar (rendered 'Belteshazzar' per standard modern biblical spelling, as with Hananiah, Mishael, Azariah in v. 17 and Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego in v. 49).
notes.2:32: Theodotion uniquely adds 'hands' (hai cheires) alongside the breast and arms of silver.
notes.2:46: Greek manna here transliterates Aramaic minchah ('grain offering/tribute'). In v. 47 the king uses plural 'your God' (hymon) for Israel's God before addressing Daniel in the singular.
notes.3:1: The Greek text (Theodotion) includes the chronological notice "In the eighteenth year," which is absent from the Aramaic Masoretic Text.
notes.3:15: The Greek term rendered "symphony" (symphonia) appears only here among the instrument lists in Theodotion (absent in 3:5, 7, 10) and may refer either to a musical ensemble or to a specific wind instrument such as a bagpipe.
notes.3:24: Verses 3:24-90 (beginning here with the Prayer of Azariah in 3:24-45) are part of the Greek text of Daniel (Theodotion) and are not found in the Aramaic Masoretic Text.
notes.3:40: The Greek phrase literally meaning "and to fulfill after You" (kai ektelesai opisthen sou) is syntactically difficult and likely reflects a Semitic idiom meaning "to wholly follow after You" (compare Numbers 14:24).
notes.3:72: In this Greek critical edition (Theodotion), the calls to "cold and heat" and "frost and snow" are grouped within 3:72 after "light and darkness," so verses 3:67-3:70 are omitted from the versification.
notes.3:92: Theodotion reads the anarthrous singular "a son of God" (huio theou), which early Christian interpreters commonly understood as a pre-incarnate appearance of the Son of God, whereas the Aramaic Masoretic Text reads plural "a son of the gods" (bar elahin).
notes.3:97: The closing clause, "and deemed them worthy to rule over all the Jews who were in his kingdom," is present in Greek Daniel (Theodotion) but absent from the Aramaic Masoretic Text.
notes.4:13: The Greek transliterates the Aramaic term for "watcher" (a wakeful heavenly being) as eir here and in 4:17, 23.
notes.4:18: Literally "a holy spirit of God"; the Greek Theodotion text also explicitly includes the name Daniel alongside Belteshazzar.
notes.4:27: The Greek text reads "perhaps God will be longsuffering toward your transgressions," differing from the Aramaic Masoretic Text ("perhaps there may be a lengthening of your prosperity").
notes.4:33: The Greek text compares Nebuchadnezzar's hair to that of lions rather than eagles' feathers as in the Aramaic Masoretic Text.
notes.4:37: In this Greek text, the royal epistolary greeting (found at 4:1-3 in the Aramaic Masoretic Text) stands at the beginning of 4:37 before Nebuchadnezzar's final doxology.
notes.5:1: The Greek text spells both King Belshazzar and Daniel's Babylonian name Belteshazzar identically as Baltasar.
notes.5:7: "Astrologers" renders the Greek loanword gazarenoi (also in 5:11), a transliteration of the Aramaic term for diviners or determiners of fate.
notes.5:11: "Watchfulness" translates Greek gregoresis, whereas the Aramaic Masoretic Text reads "light" or "illumination."
notes.5:17: The Greek inscription preserves three words (Mane, Thekel, Phares), omitting the repeated Mene and reading Phares rather than Upharsin as in the Aramaic Masoretic Text.
notes.5:27: In the Greek text, the third-person verbs and feminine participle refer to Belshazzar's kingdom ("it has been weighed... and found lacking"), rather than second-person "you" as in the Aramaic Masoretic Text.
notes.6:1: Chapter 6 in the Greek text begins with what is numbered 5:31 in the Masoretic Text, shifting the subsequent verse numbering by one through verse 15.
notes.6:15: The Greek text of Theodotion ends verse 15 here and omits verse 16 (corresponding to Masoretic 6:14b-15), proceeding directly to verse 17.
notes.6:19: Greek edesmata ("food") differs from the obscure Aramaic term often rendered "music" or "diversions"; Theodotion also includes the closing sentence "And God shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not trouble Daniel," which is absent from the Masoretic Text.
notes.6:21: Theodotion reads "with a strong voice" and "from the mouth of the lions," where the Masoretic Text reads "with a sorrowful voice" and "from the lions."
notes.7:1: Theodotion dates this vision to the "third year" of Belshazzar "king of the Chaldeans," whereas the Masoretic Text reads the "first year" of Belshazzar "king of Babylon."
notes.7:13: Theodotion reads "with the clouds of heaven" and "came up to the Ancient of Days," whereas the Old Greek reads "upon the clouds" and "came as the Ancient of Days."
notes.7:17: Theodotion interprets the four beasts as "four kingdoms" and adds "which shall be taken away," whereas the Masoretic Text reads "four kings" without the closing relative clause.
notes.7:25: The Greek verb dothesetai ("it shall be given") is singular, unlike the plural verb in the Aramaic ("they shall be given").
notes.8:2: Theodotion reads "Ubal" (Greek Oubal, transliterating the Hebrew word for "stream" or "canal") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text names the river "Ulai."
notes.8:9: Theodotion reads "one strong horn" growing toward the south and "toward the host," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "little horn" growing toward the south, the east, and the Glorious Land.
notes.8:11: Theodotion reads "even until the Chief Commander delivers the captivity; and because of him sacrifice was dashed down," a distinctive Greek rendering compared with the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.8:13: Theodotion leaves the Hebrew expression palmoni ("a certain one") untranslated as the Greek form "Phelmouni."
notes.8:25: Theodotion diverges markedly from the Hebrew Masoretic Text in this verse, reading "the yoke of his collar shall prosper," "he shall stand upon the destruction of many," and the active "like eggs he shall crush them by hand."
notes.9:8: Theodotion includes the opening confession "In You, O Lord, is our righteousness," which is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.9:24: Theodotion contains a sevenfold sequence of purposes for the seventy weeks, including the doublet "to blot out iniquities, and to make atonement for iniquities."
notes.9:25: Theodotion renders the decree as a word "to answer and to build Jerusalem" (rather than "to restore") and concludes with "and the times shall be emptied out" (rather than "in troubled times").
notes.9:26: Theodotion reads that an "anointing" (Greek chrisma) shall be utterly destroyed with "no judgment in it," and that the city and sanctuary shall be destroyed "together with the coming ruler."
notes.9:27: Theodotion includes the divine first-person pronoun "My" ("My sacrifice and drink offering shall be taken away") and reads "upon the temple" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "upon the wing."
notes.10:1: Theodotion reads "great power" (dynamis megale) joined with "understanding were given to him," whereas the Hebrew text speaks of a "great conflict."
notes.10:4: Theodotion preserves a double name for the river, combining Greek "Tigris" with the transliterated Hebrew "Eddekel" (Hiddekel).
notes.10:5: Theodotion transliterates the Hebrew term for linen garments as "baddin" here and the gemstone name as "Tarshish" in 10:6 (denoting a precious stone such as beryl or chrysolite).
notes.10:13: Theodotion reads "I left him there with the prince of the kingdom of the Persians," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "I was left there with the kings of Persia."
notes.11:1: Theodotion dates this event to "the first year of Cyrus," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the first year of Darius the Mede."
notes.11:14: Theodotion reads "the sons of the remnant" (loipon) of your people, differing from the Hebrew reading "the violent ones of your people."
notes.11:16: Theodotion transliterates the Hebrew phrase for the "glorious land" as a proper name, "Sabir" here and "Sabaein" in 11:41 and 11:45.
notes.11:31: Theodotion reads "offspring" (spermata, literally "seeds") rather than "arms" or "forces," and uses a passive participle for "a desolated abomination."
notes.11:38: Theodotion transliterates the Hebrew word for "fortresses" as the name of a deity, "the god Maozein," and similarly transliterates "palatial tents" as "Ephadano" in 11:45.
notes.12:3: The Greek text (Theodotion) reads "from among the many righteous" as a partitive expression, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "those who turn many to righteousness."
notes.12:4: The Greek text reads "the rest" (tous loipous, as in Codex Vaticanus), whereas other Greek witnesses and the Hebrew read "the words" (tous logous); likewise, "until many are taught" reflects the Greek verb rather than the Hebrew "many shall run to and fro."
notes.12:6: "Linen garments" renders the Greek transliteration ta baddein (from the Hebrew term for priestly linen), and the phrase "which you have spoken" is a reading distinctive to the Greek text.
notes.12:7: "A time of times" reflects the Greek genitive plural (kairon kairon), and the final clause follows the Greek ("when the scattering is completed, they shall know all these things") rather than the Hebrew ("when the shattering of the power of the holy people is finished, all these things shall be completed").
notes.12:13: The clause "for there are yet days until the fulfillment of the end" is a distinctive Greek reading not found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.

unplaced.text: And a decree was issued by me to bring in before me all the wise men of Babylon, so that they might make known to me the interpretation of the dream.
Then the enchanters, magicians, astrologers, and Chaldeans came in, and I myself told the dream before them; yet they did not make known its interpretation to me,
until Daniel came, whose name is Belteshazzar according to the name of my god, who has a holy spirit of God in himself; to him I said,

"Belteshazzar, chief of the enchanters, of whom I know that a holy spirit of God is in you and no mystery is beyond your ability, hear the vision of the dream which I saw, and tell me its interpretation."

And all who dwell upon the earth are accounted as nothing; and He acts according to His will in the host of heaven and in the habitation of the earth, and there is no one who can resist His hand and say to Him, "What have You done?"
I have heard concerning you that a spirit of God is in you, and watchfulness and surpassing wisdom were found in you.
And now the wise men, magicians, and astrologers came in before me to read this writing and make known its interpretation to me, yet they were not able to declare it to me.
O king, the Most High God gave the kingdom and the greatness and the honor and the glory to Nebuchadnezzar your father;

and because of the greatness which He gave him, all the peoples, tribes, and tongues trembled and feared before him; whom he wished, he slew, and whom he wished, he struck, and whom he wished, he exalted, and whom he wished, he humbled.
Yet when his heart was lifted up and his spirit grew hardened to deal arrogantly, he was brought down from the throne of the kingdom, and his honor was taken away from him,

and he was driven away from among men, and his heart was given to be with the wild beasts, and his dwelling was with wild donkeys, and they fed him grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until he knew that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of men, and to whomever He chooses, He will give it.
And you therefore, his son Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart before God; did you not know all these things?
unplaced.note: The Greek reads the rhetorical question 'did you not know all these things?' (ou panta tauta egnos) where the Aramaic reads 'even though you knew all this.'

unplaced.text: Therefore from His presence the joint of a hand was sent, and it inscribed this writing.
unplaced.note: Greek astragalos cheiros literally denotes the knuckle or joint of a hand, matching 'the joints of the hand' in 5:5.

unplaced.text: Then those men said to the king, "Know, O king, that it is the decree for Medes and Persians that no ordinance or statute which the king establishes may be altered."
